RESOLVING SUBCATEGORIES FOR GENTLE ALGEBRAS I:
MONOGENEOUS RESOLVING SUBCATEGORIES FOR GENTLE
TREES
BENJAMIN DEQUÊNE AND MICHAËL SCHOONHEERE
Abstract. Let (Q, R) be a gentle quiver such that Q is a directed tree, and K
be an algebraically closed field. We study the resolving subcategories generated
by a single nonprojective indecomposable module of KQ/⟨R⟩-mod. We modify
the geometric model of Baur–Coelho-Simões and Opper–Plamondon–Schroll
to compute such subcategories. Then we prove that these subcategories are
the join-irreducible of the poset of all the resolving subcategories ordered by
inclusion.

1. Introduction
The notion of a resolving subcategory of a module category goes back at least
to [AB69].
This notion is obtained by extracting some important properties of
the subcategory of modules of Gorenstein dimension 0: this subcategory contains
the projective modules, it is closed under direct sums, summands, extensions and
kernels of epimorphisms. The dual notion of a coresolving subcategory generalizes
the subcategory of Gorenstein injective objects.
The biresolving i.e.
resolving
and coresolving subcategories are a generalization of the subcategory of projectiveinjective objects. Inspired from the case of Frobenius categories, [Rum21] states
that, given a biresolving subcategory R of an exact category E , the localisation of
the additive quotient E /(R) at its morphisms that are both monomorphisms and
epimorphisms is triangulated.
Another natural occurrence of the contravariantly finite resolving subcategories
is through hereditary cotorsion pairs [AR91, AT22]. Hereditary cotorsion pairs are
in bijection with contravariantly finite resolving subcategories and this bijection
preserve the natural order given by inclusion. This motivates the computation of
all the contravariantly finite resolving subcategories. This question is adressed in
[Tak09] where an algorithm is given to generate the smallest resolving subcategory
R containing the family of objects X. The subcategory R is called the resolving
closure of X and denoted by Res(X). This algorithm is built to work over every
algebra of finite representation type and thus is not profiting of any potential insight
on the combinatorics on the algebra.
Gentle algebras are algebras arising from quivers with relations and appeared
for the first time in [AH81, AH82]. They have a good combinatorial behaviour: the
extension of indecomposable objects have at most two indecomposable summands
[BS80, WW85, GP68, SW83, DS87], the homspaces and extensions are endowed
with a basis following from string and band combinatorics [CB89, Kra88, ÇPS21].
Moreover the module category over the path algebra, the derived category and the
two term homotpy category of projectives are in bijection with dissected surfaces
in several geometric models [BCS19, OPS18, APS23, PPP18, PPP17] that give a
combinatorial way to compute in these categories.
Our aim is to compute the lattice of the resolving subcategories of mod A for
A a gentle algebra of finite representation type.
We first focus on the case of
gentle algebras arising from an unpunctured disc, or equivalently, the quiver of the
gentle algebra is a tree. We call monogeneous a resolving subcategory of the form
Res(X) for X an non-projective indecomposable object. Our first result concerns
the structure of the lattice of resolving subcategories.
Theorem 1.1 (5.29). The join-irreducible elements in the poset of resolving subcategories in rep(Q, R) ordered by inclusion are exactly given by the monogeneous
resolving subcategories.
